name: $33,000 to Say Yes
question: How do you cut an LLM yes/no check from $33,000 to $160 per million?
problem: A frontier LLM judge costs about $33,000 per million yes/no checks, and a sure yes looks exactly like a coin-toss yes to your if (yes).
points: Move yes/no checks off the frontier model.
Route on the probability, not on the word: above 0.95 ships, 0.6 to 0.95 goes to a person.
Give every question a "none of these" box.

stands_on.why: the check costs about as much as the work; this part makes the yes/no check cheap

title: Jev Model Explained — $33,000 vs $160 for 1M LLM-Judge Checks (TypeSafe AI's System One Model) #shorts
end_card: FRONTIER WRITES / JEV PICKS / A SYSTEM ONE MODEL · @ai.transition
caption:
Jev Model by TypeSafe AI: the first System One model. Your LLM judge costs $33,000 per 1M checks. Jev does it for $160.
AI Engineering · Part 15

Your app ships a million AI answers. Before each one goes out, a frontier judge reads answer + source and says yes or no.

At frontier prices, that one word costs $33,000 per 1M checks.

Two problems:
a) the bill grows with every answer
b) a sure yes and a coin-toss yes look the same to your if(yes)

You declare the boxes up front (yes / no), and Jev returns every box with a probability in one pass: yes 0.93, no 0.07.

In an independent test on 6,003 checks of financial-research answers, Jev agreed with the frontier judge 91.5% of the time.

Cost per 1M checks:
Frontier judge — $33,000
Cheap open model — $260
Jev — $160

Most of the saving is leaving the frontier model. What Jev adds is the number on each box. Draw a line at 0.95: above it ships, 0.6–0.95 goes to a person.

The limit: it always picks one of your boxes. Testers sent 30 messages that fit no box. A cake recipe came back as "technical issue, 0.94". 0 of 30 flagged. It can't return a wrong type. It can return a wrong answer in the right type.

RULE 1: Move yes/no checks off the frontier model.
RULE 2: Route on the probability, not on the word.
RULE 3: Give every question a "none of these" box.

Sources and numbers in the open vault, link in bio.

Next part: how many labelled examples you need to place that 0.95 line.
